Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings:  27-year-old woman with 2 days of constant dull suprapubic pain, nausea, subjective fever, increased urinary frequency, and recent inter-menstrual spotting. No dysuria, urgency, vomiting, diarrhoea, or vaginal discharge. On etonogestrel implant.  
- Working diagnosis:  Lower-abdominal/pelvic pain – rule out urinary tract infection versus early pregnancy (including ectopic) versus pelvic inflammatory disease.  
- Supporting DDx (consistent with transcript):  
  • Urinary tract infection – high likelihood given suprapubic ache, urinary frequency, nausea, subjective fever despite absent dysuria.  
  • Early intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy – medium likelihood; spotting and pelvic pain near expected menses; contraception reduces but does not eliminate risk.  
  • Pelvic inflammatory disease – medium likelihood owing to pain, systemic symptoms, spotting, sexual activity.  
- Management plan:  
  • Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for physical examination (including abdominal and pelvic exam).  
  • Point-of-care pregnancy test; consider serum β-hCG if needed to exclude ectopic.  
  • Urinalysis ± urine culture to assess for UTI.  
  • STI screening (NAAT for Chlamydia/Gonorrhoea) and pelvic swabs if PID suspected.  
  • Blood tests (FBC, CRP) if systemic infection suspected.  
  • Provide red-flag advice: seek urgent care if pain worsens, feels faint, develops heavy bleeding, or other concerning symptoms.  
  • Allergy alert: Amoxicillin – avoid penicillins if antibiotics required.

3. Pelvic inflammatory disease – Medium likelihood: lower-abdominal pain, spotting, systemic symptoms in sexually active woman.
